decisions.executionNote: Approach the nearest objects from above with both arms in their own workspace; gradually turn grippers downward while preserving elbow continuity.
Previous command was rejected without motion. Use much smaller initial pose increments to leave the initial configuration continuously.
Aim left gripper above the left watch and right gripper above the white chocolate wrapper. Complete most of the downward rotation at safe height.
Finish vertical alignment over the left watch and right white chocolate bar, descending slowly while open; grasp height remains visually uncertain.
Replan from measured poses after interruption, using smaller translations to finish downward orientation and align with objects.
Refine alignment using a higher table-plane estimate and finish vertical gripper attitude slowly; keep open pending a clear view.
Lower slowly toward watch and wrapper while correcting near-vertical orientation. Red car has shifted near the right grasp, so inspect before closing.
Contact suggests a higher support plane. Relieve downward load, shift left grasp toward watch center, and lift right away from overlapping car and wrapper.
Fine-adjust the left watch grasp from wrist RGB and close; bring right gripper above the unobstructed rightmost watch.
Lift left watch to test retention. Center rightmost watch between jaw tips using wrist image and close without further downward pressure.
Left watch stayed on the table. Reopen and bring the band centers deeper between the jaws; adjust right alignment similarly before another grasp.
Close around the visually centered watch bands, pause for closure, and lift both vertically to verify retention.
Left watch is visibly retained; carry it toward the left side of the middle basket. Right watch remained on the table, so reopen and recenter it nearer the jaw tips.
Continue toward middle basket with smaller increments after the continuity guard. Keep the held watch closed; lower right around its watch at corrected alignment.
Tilt the retained watch forward to reach the middle basket without further wrist extension. Adjust right watch grasp toward the jaw tips and close.
Move the held left watch inside the middle basket and release. Lift the right watch vertically to check retention before transporting.
Release the retained watch over the middle basket without further extension and retreat. Right watch was not retained; reopen and align its band nearer the jaw tips.
Middle basket visibly contains the left watch. Approach the red chocolate wrapper with left arm; shift right grasp slightly back to capture the watch band at the jaw tips.
Grasp the centered red chocolate wrapper with left arm and test-lift it. Lift the right watch, then begin a conservative inward transit while keeping it closed.
Carry the right watch toward the middle basket with a forward tilt. Bring left chocolate toward a central staging spot for right-arm pickup, without crossing arms.
Right watch is retained: move it over the middle basket, not the red basket. Left chocolate slipped; return open over its new location for a deeper grasp.
Release the right watch inside the middle basket, then withdraw toward the remaining watch. Center left chocolate longitudinally and close at a slightly lower height.
Both placed watches are visible in the middle basket. Retreat right with smaller continuity-safe increments; refine and close the left chocolate grasp.
Lift the grasped chocolate and start moving toward a central transfer spot. Bring the right gripper down toward the final tabletop watch, staying open until aligned.
Lower the retained chocolate onto a central left-side staging spot for later right-arm transfer. Close and lift the remaining watch to verify grasp.
Carry the retained final watch toward the middle basket with forward tilt. Clear the central area with left arm; chocolate slipped onto the table and needs regrasping.
Release final watch over the middle basket, then approach right white chocolate. Bring left gripper over the yellow-wrapped chocolate, keeping the arms separated.
Center the yellow and white chocolate wrappers between each gripper's jaws, close at tabletop grasp height, and inspect before lifting.
Lift both chocolate grasp attempts vertically and inspect RGB retention before committing to transfer or basket placement.
Dove wrapper is retained in left gripper; carry toward central transfer area. White wrapper remained on table, so reopen right and lower for a deeper centered grasp.
Dove slipped during transit. Return left to its new table position; lower right slightly more and close across the white wrapper center.
Align the left jaws across the diagonal Dove wrapper before closing. Lift the deeper right white-wrapper grasp gently to check retention.
Thin wrappers appear to slip from shallow grasps. Reopen and lower jaw contact carefully before reclosing left; approach white wrapper at the same deeper height.
Relieve tabletop contact by lifting the left grasp. Close right at the measured height and test a slow lift, avoiding additional downward loading.
Carry securely centered Dove slowly toward a central staging point. Right wrapper appears unretained and obstructed by the car; move above the car to separate it first.
Continue left chocolate to the central boundary while held securely. Align right jaws across the red car, maintaining arm separation and a safe approach height.
Lower Dove at a clear central boundary staging spot. Right gripper has contacted the basket area; retreat up and back before attempting another object grasp.
Release Dove onto the central boundary for a later right-arm pickup and retreat left. Approach the yellow car with right gripper open.
Approach red chocolate at its new position with left arm. Align right jaws across the yellow car's narrow body and close, keeping it separate from the baskets.
Refine red-wrapper centering and close left. Complete right closure and lift the yellow car to verify whether the body is securely retained.
Car stayed on table, suggesting a shallow grasp. Reopen and approach lower at its updated orientation. Complete left closure and lift the red wrapper for retention check.
Close right around the now-centered yellow car at lower height and test-lift. Reopen left and return for a better centered, deeper red-wrapper grasp.
Yellow car is visibly retained. Carry it toward a central right-side transfer spot without crossing arms. Close and lift the centered red wrapper with left.
Stage the retained car at the central front area for left-arm pickup, and the red wrapper farther back for right-arm pickup. Maintain separated paths and closed grips.
Release the car at the central transfer spot and withdraw right. Move the red wrapper slightly away from the robot base before releasing onto the table.
The car and wrappers are staged on the table. Route left around the left side toward the car and right around its side toward Dove, keeping the arms separated.
Tracking residuals and RGB indicate the wrists are too close. Separate outward and upward on each side before planning independent approaches.
Use staggered front/back approaches: left toward the staged car, right toward the rear red chocolate. Correct gripper attitudes while maintaining separation.
Center the upside-down car in the left jaws and the red wrapper in the right jaws, using wrist RGB while staying on each side of the central boundary.
Fine-adjust both grasps away from excess contact, then close and test a short vertical lift. Keep right EE on its own side while grasping the boundary wrapper.
Carry the visibly grasped yellow car toward the left basket with a gradual forward tilt. Lift and move the red-wrapper attempt slightly right to assess retention.
Lift the retained car up and back from the blue basket before continuing left. Reapproach the red wrapper with a small inward gripper tilt while keeping right EE on its side.
Carry the yellow car over the left basket with clearance and a modest forward tilt. Close the better-centered right wrapper grasp and begin a gentle test lift.
Release the car into the left basket and retreat. Reopen the right red-wrapper attempt and retry at a slightly deeper contact height without crossing the central boundary.
Lift the deeper red-wrapper grasp slowly. Retreat left to clear the basket view and verify where the released car settled.
Car appears behind the white basket rather than inside; cautiously approach for a clearer view without overextension. Recenter and lower the right wrapper grasp while open.
Raise and lean the left gripper over the basket's rear wall toward the misplaced car, with small reach increments. Recenter and close right on the red wrapper.
Refine left approach using the now-visible car behind the basket, moving back and down rather than extending farther. Test-lift the centered red wrapper slowly.
Approach the misplaced car cautiously from above the rear rim. Reopen right and move the thin wrapper closer to the jaw-tip contact region for a more reliable pinch.
Clear the left basket rim by lifting and using a steeper approach toward the car. Close right on the wrapper now aligned with jaw tips, then test-lift.
Red wrapper is visibly retained; carry it slowly toward the right basket. Lower left cautiously onto the car behind the basket and attempt a grasp.
Lift left to check whether the car is actually retained. Carry the held red chocolate toward the front interior of the right basket, avoiding an overshoot beyond its rear rim.
Both grasps were lost. Use a steeper left approach over the rear rim, and reapproach the red wrapper now in the right workspace. Avoid rotating thin wrappers during the next carry.
After the guard, hold left orientation and reduce height instead of extending farther. Approach the right red wrapper with smaller increments and restore a near-vertical pinch.
Refine the left car pinch slightly forward, left, and lower. Close right on the centered red wrapper and lift without changing orientation.
The pinches appear too shallow. Lower the left approach to contact the car body beneath the roof and lower the right wrapper grasp carefully, inspecting contact before transport.
Lift left to relieve contact and test the deeper car grasp. Close right at the deeper wrapper height, pause, and lift without changing attitude.
Right appears to hold both chocolate wrappers. Lift and carry toward the red basket with only a very gradual tilt. Withdraw left from the continuity limit; the car stayed behind the basket.
Carry the remaining red wrapper higher over the basket rim with a very gradual tilt. Move left outward to explore a side approach around the white basket rather than contacting its rear wall.
Release red chocolate inside the right basket and withdraw. Continue a slow left-side approach toward the misplaced car, keeping the gripper clear of the white basket wall.
Finish releasing the red wrapper and withdraw right. Replan left away from its joint-limit region with smaller backward and downward increments; do not continue the rejected reach.

Red wrapper is inside the right basket. Approach the remaining white wrapper above the red car; use the left gripper's diagonal reach toward the yellow car while maintaining its elbow-up configuration.
Left is contacting the basket rim; lift and back off while adjusting the diagonal approach. Center the white chocolate near the right jaw tips and close above the car.
Lower the left diagonal approach toward the car body while watching rim clearance. Lift the white wrapper vertically to verify retention before carrying it over the red basket.
Refine the left diagonal reach toward the car, accounting for the shorter fingertip offset. White wrapper was not retained; reopen and reapproach its updated position.
Left approach is blocked by the basket wall; withdraw from contact rather than pushing through. Move the right pinch back from the red rim and close on the exposed white-wrapper end.
Previous retreat executed nothing. Bridge the left observed and preceding target attitudes with tiny increments, then slowly relieve contact; make only a small right grasp adjustment.
Lift the right wrapper pinch away from the car and rim. Raise and shift the left approach toward the visible car without descending into the basket wall.
Rotate the left jaws about their approach axis to grasp across the car's width rather than length. Reapproach white chocolate slightly farther back for a centered pinch.
Complete left jaw alignment across the car and lower gradually. Center the white wrapper on the right jaw-tip contact region and close.
Test-lift the right white wrapper. Close left and withdraw gently from the obstructing rim, checking whether the car or rim is engaged rather than continuing to press downward.

White wrapper appears retained; carry it slowly over the red basket rim. Withdraw left from the obstructed car and gradually return its gripper toward a tabletop approach for the remaining Dove wrapper.
